column1: E-C04 cost democratization - cost per full all-pairs screen and per statistically verified candidate
All timings measured on this workstation (i7 + RTX 3060 Ti, C++ Release).
Power assumptions: RTX 3060 Ti board cap 225 W (count kernel phases, NVML unavailable - TDP bound);
CPU package 95 W (Fisher/stats phase is CPU-bound single process). Electricity $0.15/kWh residential.
Cloud CPU cluster baseline: 8 x c6i.2xlarge (8 vCPU, $0.34/h on-demand us-east-1), count phase row-sliced
(1/8 work per node, byte-identical slices verified in E-C02/E-C05) + 15% parallel overhead;
Fisher phase single node. Datacenter-GPU rental quoted at ~$1.10/h (A100 marketplace median) for context.

pairs tested 29,889,274 (c11>=2 scope) | Bonferroni-significant 1,484,134 | threshold 2.89e-11

HEADLINE NUMBERS (Figure 4 core):
- Full all-pairs significant-pair screen of a 2,000-genome prokaryotic pangenome:
< 95 s wall-clock and ~1.3 US cents of electricity on a single $400 consumer GPU.
- Cost per statistically verified candidate pair: ~1e-9 US$ (consumer) vs ~1.4e-8 US$
(cloud CPU cluster baseline) - a ~10x democratization factor, before counting the
capital barrier (GPU instance quota/price vs commodity card).
- Screen (hypergeometric deviation) is lossless on real data: output byte-identical
to exhaustive c11>=2 enumeration (E-C05), so no candidate is lost for the 4.5x
count speedup.
NOTES: Fisher phase dominates wall-clock (67-71%); it is embarrassingly parallel over
pairs (independent 2x2 tests), so GPU-resident Fisher (future work) would push the full
pipeline under 30 s. $/candidate scales inversely with cohort density of significant
pairs; denominators above are cohort-specific.
